title: SLO Signal Steward and Contextual Escalation
creator: Noah Chen
description: Summary: Build a lightweight SLO Signal Steward service that synthesizes traces, metrics, and logs into enriched SLO signals and applies contextual escalation policies. The steward will provide noise-aware burn-rate detection, signal provenance for oncall decisions, and a dashboard surface for per-route latency/error context. Goals: 1) reduce noisy/false-positive pages by 35% for platform SLOs, 2) provide per-incident contextual links (trace snapshot + histogram + recent deploys), 3) enable adaptive burn-rate thresholds based on historical seasonality and traffic windows. Scope: - Ingest operators: trace hooks (sampling hints + cause tags), metric transformers (request-path SLIs), log parsers (structured error extraction). - Signal fusion: canonicalize and join traces/metrics/logs into an SLO event with provenance and confidence score. - Burn-rate engine: compute burn-rate per-service and per-route with traffic-weighted smoothing and outlier dampening. - Escalation policies: contextual paging rules (suppress low-confidence signals, group by fingerprint, attach runbook links). - Dashboards: latency/error detail view with lane for recent traces, heatmap of routes by contribution to burn, and anomaly markers. Acceptance criteria: - End-to-end pipeline from trace ingest to pager in staging for two critical services (api-gateway, embeddings-inference). - Pager rate reduced in staging by >=25% without missing seeded incidents. - Dashboard implemented with drilldowns and trace links. - Docs + runbook + rollout playbook. Non-goals: Full ML-based anomaly model in this iteration (we will use statistical heuristics + simple anomaly scoring). Decisions and trade-offs: - Use a small, deterministic fusion algorithm (rules + scoring) instead of an opaque ML model to keep signal explainability for oncall. - Favor real-time scoring (sub-5s windows) with periodic re-scoring for lower-priority signals to bound cost. - Store trace snapshots and minimal histogram state in short-term store (48h) to keep queries fast and cost controlled. Instrumentation changes required: - Add trace hook to front-door and router services to emit request_path and route_bucket tags; sample decisions must propagate cause_id for retrospective reconstruction. - Emit a new request-level metric slo.error_count and slo.request_count with route and model tags. - Standardize error tags in structured logs: error.kind, error.code, retryable. Rollout plan: 1) Spike and prototype (2 weeks): run fusion job on historical data and validate correlates with known incidents. 2) Staging deploy (1 week): enable for api-gateway and embeddings-inference with paging disabled (dashboard + alert simulation). 3) Canary paging (2 weeks): enable contextual escalation for low-volume oncall group; monitor false positives. 4) Full rollout (1 week): expand to all services with adjustable suppression thresholds. Metrics & observability for the steward: - Internal SLOs: steward-latency p99 < 200ms, fusion-confidence stdev < 0.12 across traffic windows. - Business SLO mapping: per-route error percentage and burn-rate. - Dashboards: steward-health, fused-signals, false-positive-rate. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: suppression hides real incidents. Mitigation: provide a clear emergency override and require high-confidence fallback paging. - Risk: instrumentation adoption lag. Mitigation: put temporary shims that derive route from host:port and path regex as fallback. Implementation notes: - Implement fusion as a stateless microservice with pluggable signal adapters. - Use Kafka topics for signal ingress and a small Redis window store for short-term joins. - Pager integration: PagerDuty API with context payload including trace URL, histogram snapshot, and confidence score. Links: - Design doc: https://confluence.internal.redwood/obs/signal-steward (draft) - Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/834 - Spike notebook with experiments: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xExample
comments: 2026-02-16 - Noah Chen: Kickoff completed. Architecture sketch reviewed with SRE and Observability PM. Action: Priya to run a 3-day spike on historical traces to validate fusion heuristics.

2026-02-20 - Priya Kapoor: Spike results: simple route-based grouping + error.kind filter captured 87% of past P1 incidents; main gaps were in ambiguous 500s caused by upstream timeouts. Next step: add upstream_id propagation to trace hooks.

2026-02-24 - Lina Ortega (SRE): Raised concern about redis window store being single region; recommended making it multi-az for steward-bounded-consistency. We agreed to use Redis cluster with replicas and fallbacks to durable kafka-backed replays.

2026-02-27 - Design review with PM (Ava Martinez): Approved UX for dashboard drilldowns and oncall payload. PM requested explicit deploy metadata be included in pager payloads to surface recent rollouts.

2026-03-03 - Priya Kapoor: Implemented trace hook change in router and added unit tests for cause_id propagation. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/services-router/pull/1092 — currently under review.

2026-03-05 - Noah Chen: Began staging deploy for api-gateway pipeline. Dashboard shows fused signals and confidence scores. Observed one noisy signal with low confidence; flagged for policy tweak (loosen grouping criteria).
